nominations.basis: Probed with scripts/probe_candidate_pages.py on 2026-09-18: this is the United States Government Manual's Department of State entry (the official handbook of the federal government, published by NARA's Office of the Federal Register), it answers robots.txt and reads with 46,537 characters of text outside the chrome, and the verifier's own label test returns labelled for this node with matchedText "Foreign Service Institute" in the page CONTENT, not the site-wide chrome. It is a directory entry for the parent department rather than FSI's own site -- FSI's own pages are on www.state.gov, which answers robots.txt 403 and is refused, and fsi.state.gov does not resolve -- so the role is official_list; note for the reviewer that promote files every role under the node's own id, so a confirmation from it would publish the own-page method string. Confidence stays likely because verify_base_graph.py re-fetches and decides for itself.

The mission's own host usun.usmission.gov answers robots.txt 403 and is refused, as do usun.state.gov, www.usmission.gov and geneva.usmission.gov, and www.usun.gov does not resolve, so this directory entry is the only readable page found that names the unit; role official_list because it is a government directory's entry for the parent department, not the mission's own site.

note: Correcting the earlier no_public_page_known on this node: the obstacle that reason rested on -- that the only page obliged to list this committee's subcommittees (https://cha.house.gov/subcommittees) carries 229 characters outside its chrome and so falls below this project's 400-character readable floor, which I re-probed on 2026-09-18 and confirm -- is not the only such page. The House Clerk's own committee list at https://clerk.house.gov/committees reads with 5,257 characters and 620 label fragments, and it is the complete official list (the same list this repository already keeps as tests/fixtures/directories/house/committees.xlsx). It labels 'Committee on House Administration' in content and, beneath it, exactly two subcommittee labels: 'Elections' and 'Modernization and Innovation'. Nothing on it equals or folds to 'Subcommittee on Committees'. That is the page's own wording, and it is what a curator should act on: the graph carries leg-house-cmte-house-administration-sub-elections for the first and has no node at all for the second, so the fix here is curation -- rename this node to the Modernization and Innovation subcommittee or drop it -- not another URL. Worth noting that no URL could confirm it in any case: committee_core_key folds this node's name to the single token 'Committees', and the fold requires two or more tokens to be granted, so even a page printing the word could not confirm it.
